display.title: Episode 475: The Flickering Flame (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show without music: respect for others, the value of each day, a shoemaker's words 'as long as the candle burns, one can still repair,' and Moshe Rabbeinu's humility before Shavuos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefirah, 5751, without music. Uncle Yossi explains that we avoid music now because Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague for not showing respect to one another, so these are days to honor parents, teachers and friends, look for the good in others and pursue peace. Counting the Omer teaches that each day must be better than the one before, and that time is a precious gift never to be wasted. A young yeshiva student recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of Rabbi Yisroel, stranded in a snowstorm, who finds a light in a shoemaker's window late at night. The old man explains he poured too much oil into his lamp, and 'as long as the light still burns, one can still repair.' Rabbi Yisroel hears in this a lesson about teshuvah: as long as a person lives, he can still repair. Before Shavuos, Uncle Yossi teaches that the Torah was given to the humblest of men on the lowest mountain, as the Alter Rebbe explains 'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai.' The show ends with an invitation to sign up friends for Tzivos Hashem and the candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: As long as the candle burns, we can still repair: use every day for Torah, mitzvos and teshuvah, show respect to others, and stay humble like Moshe Rabbeinu.

date.note: Days of Sefirah, before Shavuos; Shabbos candles 7:21 fits Friday 19 April 1991 in New York, one week after episode 474.
